name: Highlands 6

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a large multi-wing residence situated on a graded, elevated pad near the center of a large desert scrub parcel|A paved driveway connects from the road at the upper portion of the image, curving down and around the structure to a circular motor court on the right side of the home|To the left of the main structure, a putting green and a hard-surface tennis court are visible, surrounded by low desert scrub and scattered conifers|The property is set back significantly from the paved road, with the driveway being the sole defined access route into the site.

alpha.desc: The alpha view highlights the front of the residence from a northwest-facing perspective, showing the multi-gabled, multi-wing roofline of the main structure and the curved driveway approaching from the upper right|The paved road runs along the right edge of the parcel, and the driveway entrance connects to that road before sweeping across the graded pad toward the motor court|Scattered conifer trees are present along the perimeter of the landscaped zone near the structure|The surrounding terrain is open desert with no fencing or walls visible at the property boundary.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, revealing the full extent of the curved driveway as it approaches the main structure from the road at the upper left|The putting green area is visible on the left side of the structure, and the tennis court is positioned to the rear-left of the main building|The right side of the residence shows multiple roof wings with a complex roofline, and the motor court area is identifiable near the front-right of the building mass|The terrain between the road and the structure is open, graded desert with minimal vegetation.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the residence, with a small pool or water feature visible adjacent to the putting green on the left side of the structure|The rear elevation of the home presents a complex, multi-peaked roofline with no clearly defined secondary access routes or outbuildings visible from this angle|The road and a road intersection are visible in the lower left of the frame, separated from the structure by a large expanse of open desert terrain|No fencing, gates, or barriers are observed between the rear of the structure and the surrounding open land.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, with the putting green and pool or water feature clearly visible adjacent to the left wing of the residence|The main driveway curves around the front of the structure and is visible from this angle approaching from the lower right where the paved road runs|The left side of the structure has direct open ground access with no fencing or obstacles separating it from the surrounding desert|Sparse conifer trees are positioned near the structure on this side.

considerations: The property is accessed by a single paved driveway that originates from a curving road and travels a significant distance across open terrain before reaching the motor court at the front of the residence. The large open graded pad surrounding the structure provides substantial staging and positioning area for emergency vehicles on multiple sides. The complex, multi-wing roofline and multiple building sections increase the overall structure footprint and may complicate interior orientation for responders. No fencing, gates, or barriers are visible along the driveway route or around the perimeter of the structure.
clarifications: Is there a gate or access control at the driveway entrance from the road, and if so, what is the entry method? Are there additional pedestrian or secondary vehicle access points to the structure beyond the main driveway? What is the surface composition of the motor court and surrounding pad — is it paved or compacted gravel — and will it support the weight of heavy emergency apparatus? Are there propane tanks or other fuel storage locations on the property not visible from the roof-level imagery? Does the pool or water feature adjacent to the putting green have a dedicated access point for water supply operations?
